text:
Anya K: Quick question — are we comfortable with the current overlay eviction behavior when a prefix is shared across multiple tenants? I just hit a repro where handoff + soft-evict caused two replicas to serve the same prefix for ~800ms and it confused the caller retry logic.

Rob P: Oof. Can you paste the minimal repro or logs? My first guess is lease/state divergence during a demote+handoff window.

Anya K: Here's the smol log snippet from the runner:
```
[6066667777] pref-mgr: soft-evict start prefix=/users/abc epoch=42
[6066667782] handoff-coord: request-handoff prefix=/users/abc -> nodeB token=tok123
[6066667789] nodeB: accept-handoff prefix=/users/abc token=tok123 epoch=43
[6066667794] nodeA: soft-evict finished but still serving while waiting for lease-revoke ack
```
Rob P: Looks like nodeA continued to honor existing in-memory residency until explicit token-revoke. The race is: handoff completes on nodeB before nodeA fully demotes local hot flag. NodeA still answers because it thinks it's entitled.

Taylor L: This matches earlier weirdness. We intentionally allowed a grace window for in-flight requests during soft-evict to avoid spikes, but we didn't bound the window by the handoff token. So overlap is expected but normally short. 800ms is long but plausible under GC pauses.

Samir: Two options: 1) make handoff atomic by introducing a single authoritative ownership token exchange (nodeB must get token and only then nodeA stops serving), or 2) keep current overlap but make responses include a forwarding hint so callers retry to the new owner. Both have tradeoffs.

Anya K: I worry about option 1) increased latency at handoff (we'd block handoff until nodeA drains) and complexity of distributed consensus for token transfer. Option 2) is lighter but pushes complexity to callers and breaks current client semantics.

Rob P: Another hybrid: define a strict short window (eg 50ms) where both may serve, and after that any in-memory serving must verify token validity from a local fast cache. If missing, return a special 409/evict hint. That reduces long tails without global sync.

Taylor L: Implementation sketch:
- introduce owner_epoch and owner_token in prefix metadata
- on handoff: nodeB acquires new owner_token and owner_epoch (persisted), then nodeA is signalled to demote
- nodeA can serve if its local owner_epoch == prefix.owner_epoch || serve_age < soft_grace_ms
- otherwise respond with `X-Prefix-Redirect: owner=nodeB` header (or internal error code)

Samir: That feels reasonable. Need to be careful: when nodeB gets token early (before nodeA demotes) we still have overlap but nodeB can accept requests and nodeA will stop after soft_grace_ms or token mismatch. So ordering: persist on central coord -> nodeB can start -> nodeA demotes async.

Anya K: We must also consider multi-tenant sharing: two tenants might map to same physical prefix (hotkey sharing). Our owner_token must be tenant-scoped to avoid cross-tenant steals. Add tenant_id to token.

Rob P: Agreed. Also add telemetry: counters for overlap_serves, token_mismatch_rejects, redirect_hints_emitted. That will let us tune soft_grace_ms.

Taylor L: Test matrix:
- handoff success where nodeA drains within soft_grace_ms (no client-visible change)
- handoff where nodeA GC pauses and exceeds soft_grace_ms -> callers get redirect/409 then retry to new owner
- simultaneous handoff churn across N nodes
- multi-tenant prefix aliasing where token tenant mismatch must reject

Samir: For canary, we can start by returning redirect hints only (non-fatal). Clients that are rollout-aware will follow hint. After 2 weeks/metrics we flip to hard rejects when mismatch occurs.

Anya K: Action items:
- Taylor: draft small RFC with the owner_token + soft_grace semantics and metrics, include pseudocode + tests (owner: Taylor)
- Rob: add telemetry hooks and a dashboard sketch (owner: Rob)
- Samir: add canary plan and client-compat checklist (owner: Samir)
- Anya: small reproducible harness and the failing logs attached to the RFC (owner: Anya)

Rob P: ack. One more nit: make sure lease-bot/lease-manager is the single source-of-truth for token issuance (avoid two independent coordinators).

lease-bot: noted: token_issuer = lease-manager.emit_token(prefix, tenant_id) -> returns token+epoch. All actions must be idempotent.

Taylor L: I'll aim to have the RFC draft by EOD Friday. Will include a fallback switch gated by a remote flag.

Anya K: Thanks team — this plan keeps correctness tight while allowing a gradual rollout. I'll attach the harness to the RFC. :thumbsup:
